name: Plan VFX
description: Plans visual effects enhancements for specific clips.

inputs.name: creative_brief
inputs.description: The captain's creative direction as markdown, injected by the runner from the project's creative_brief path. Empty when the project declares none.

inputs.name: project_context
inputs.description: The project's context folder plus the learnings routed to this step, as a MAP the model follows with its shell (never a copy). Injected by the runner from the project's context/ folder and learned_context/ store when this step declares it; a stated absence when the project has neither. See library/tools/project_context.py.

inputs.name: clip_catalog
inputs.description: State input: clip_catalog. Read for the clip_id the rest of this step's context uses; `view:picture` keys its rows by it. Optional because the view names the vision pass's own id and says so when no clip list is routed.

inputs.name: timeline_notes
inputs.description: The captain's own notes typed onto the built timeline in DaVinci Resolve, routed to this step because this step owns the decision each note is about. Injected by the runner from <project>/marker_feedback/ and absent when there are none. See library/tools/marker_routing.py.

inputs.name: prosody_analysis
inputs.description: State input: prosody_analysis. Read through view:emphasis only - the per-block most-emphasized words a punch or shake may anchor to. Optional because a run that measured no prosody still plans; the view states the absence in one line.

outputs.name: enhancement_spec
outputs.description: State output: enhancement_spec. `visual_effects` is the resolved plan; `planning_basis` says why it is the length it is, so an empty plan the planner chose is distinguishable from one whose every entry was dropped. See library/tools/vfx_plan_basis.py.

llm_outputs.name: vfx_creative
llm_outputs.description: Visual effects, at most one per block. Each: target_block_position, effect_type, params, rationale. Drift motion on a static hold (`slow_zoom_in` / `slow_zoom_out`, or `ken_burns` with the direction read off `zoom_start`/`zoom_end`) applies ONLY where the entry states a per-shot rationale saying why that shot wants it - an entry with a missing or blank rationale gets no motion and is dropped as `no_stated_reason` (captain's ruling 2026-09-08; motion is never a blanket rule or a default). A `ken_burns` entry whose params state no direction (`zoom_end` equal to `zoom_start`, or either missing) is dropped as `ken_burns_without_direction` - the direction is derived, never defaulted. `stabilize` is the one corrective treatment: it runs Resolve's own Stabilize on the clip (judged by its return) and takes no params - name it only where the measured stability in context (`view:stability`, the candidate table's camera text) says the shot needs it; nothing stabilizes unless the plan asks (captain, 2026-09-24). OPTIONAL anchor / anchor_end name the effect's sub-block span (a word, beat/downbeat/bar or frame inside the block, with optional offset_seconds/offset_frames; a punch spanning one word anchors the word's start and its end). Either alone leaves the other end on the block boundary; an unresolvable anchor refuses the step.
